bindings.label: Patient presented with cough and low fever for one day

A 63-year-old male was admitted to the Emergency Department; one day before admission, he experienced paroxysmal cough with a small amount of thick white sputum, chills, fever (max 37.9°C), dizziness, general pain including mild headache and continuous throbbing pain at the top of the head without nausea/vomiting, and poor appetite.
Past medical history includes hypertension with highest BP 165/95 mmHg, unknown disease control status, and no treatment.

Physical examination: temperature 37.3°C, pulse 70 bpm, respiratory rate 22 bpm, blood pressure 125/75 mmHg, SpO2 98% on room air; patient appeared acutely ill with clear consciousness, spontaneous positioning, no lip cyanosis, no mouth angle deviation, soft neck without resistance, moist rales in both lower lungs, regular heart rhythm without murmur, soft abdomen, no lower extremity swelling, and negative pathological signs.
Laboratory tests show elevated white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, and neutrophil percentage
Chest CT shows bronchial disease and multiple exudates in both lungs
Myocardial enzymes, D-dimer, and NT-proBNP are elevated
Sputum culture, blood culture, procalcitonin, and respiratory pathogen PCR are not yet available
